The federal court will likely remand the case because the woman, as the plaintiff, cannot remove her own case to federal court—removal is available only to defendants under 28 U.S.C. § 1441. Even though federal-question jurisdiction exists, the plaintiff's voluntary filing in state court and her status as the party seeking removal bar the procedure. The attorney's motive to avoid the judge is irrelevant to the removal analysis.

CONFIDENCE: 97
